# Funded round 1 of 2 for Task 1, then hard stop on funded `STAGNANT`

**Fixed state**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Owning checkout | `/workspace/project` |
| Wave | 1, with `### Task 1:` and `### Task 2:` |
| `WAVE_BASE_SHA` | `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` |
| Task 1 counters | `failed[1] ≥ 2`, `escalated[1]` set and spent |
| Grant | 2 funded rounds, 0 spent |
| Tracker | Both indices stay `in_progress` |
| Phase | `implement` |

I assume Task 1's manifest mode is isolated, because no `"mode":"in-place"` was supplied.

**Placeholders**

- `<REPORT_DIR>`, `<Artifacts dir>` and `<RP_TREE>` are values the tools print.
- `<TASK1_TESTS>` and `<WAVE_TESTS>` are the manifest `tests` arrays, kept verbatim.
- `<PRIOR_REVIEW_REPORT>` and `<TREE_PREV>` come from the last transcript line `wave 1 review <k> verdict FIX_FIRST report <path> tree <sha>`.

## 1. Resolve `implModel` (stop if undefined or the tool is unavailable)

```ts
gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })
```

## 2. Snapshot the current integrated tree (repair-base recipe)

<!-- repair-base-shell -->
```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE='1111111111111111111111111111111111111111'
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1; fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

## 3. Record spending before dispatch, then dispatch

Print this line before the dispatch. It is the only line that records spending on resume:

```text
funded round 1 of 2 for task 1
```

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<RP_TREE>", model: "<implModel>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_1", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave1-task1-funded1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules>; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <TASK1_TESTS>.\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<PRIOR_REVIEW_REPORT>\nRead it yourself. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

The carrier deliberately has no `context: "fresh"` and no prior-patch path. It repeats the escalated payload: same model, same tree, same anchors.

## 4. Integrate the delta (observed status: `DONE`)

```bash
test -s '<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch'
git -C /workspace/project apply --index '<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch'
```

Then print:

```text
wave 1 repair <k> task 1 DONE report <REPORT_DIR>/wave1-task1-funded1.md delta <patch> applied yes
```

Remove the snapshot tree:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project worktree remove --force '<RP_TREE>'
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

## 5. Record the new tree and check the delta is non-empty

Run the fix-delta block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'`. It prints `<TREE_NEW>`. Then:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <TREE_PREV> <TREE_NEW>
```

## 6. Gate on Task 1's tests (observed: green)

Run each command in `<TASK1_TESTS>` separately:

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && <test i>) > gate-<i>.log 2>&1; echo "wave 1 gate <i> exit $?"
```

## 7. Re-review

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer", output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave1-review<k+1>.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: [### Task 1:, ### Task 2:]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <WAVE_TESTS>.\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<PRIOR_REVIEW_REPORT>\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <TREE_PREV>\ntree-after: <TREE_NEW>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <TREE_PREV> <TREE_NEW> yourself. Apply the trajectory block." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

Print:

```text
wave 1 review <k+1> verdict FIX_FIRST report <REPORT_DIR>/wave1-review<k+1>.md tree <TREE_NEW>
```

## 8. Observed `FIX_FIRST` with `TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT` → hard stop

A funded re-review that returns `STAGNANT` stops immediately, even though funded round 2 remains.

- No second funded round.
- No re-dispatch to obtain the trajectory line.
- No commit.
- Both tracker indices stay `in_progress`.
- The phase stays `implement`.

For the residual findings, I do one bounded read, then write the stop note:

```ts
read({ path: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave1-review<k+1>.md", limit: 300 })
```

Stop note template. The quoted lines come only from that read; I invent no finding:

```text
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 1 (<title>); escalated round on <implModel> did not resolve it.

Problem: <the STAGNANT repeat finding, one sentence>
budget: 1 of 2 spent
  <file:line> - <quoted residual finding>

Fix options:
  a) <concrete change>
  b) amend spec section <X> / plan task 1 <...>

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: <option> - <why>
```

## Resume: transcript present vs. missing

| Transcript on resume | Spent recovered | Budget line | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| `funded round 1 of 2 for task 1` plus the `applied yes` repair line and the `STAGNANT` review line | 1 | `budget: 1 of 2 spent` | Stop stands. `STAGNANT` stops regardless of the remaining round. Wait for the human. |
| `funded round` line present, but no terminal review or green gate after it | 1 (spending is recorded before dispatch) | `budget: 1 of 2 spent` | Stop note. Never infer the outcome or re-dispatch the interrupted worker. |
| No `funded round` line | Not recoverable, treated as exhausted | `budget: 2 of 2 spent (not recovered on resume)` | No funded round. Stop note. The budget never resets to zero. |
| Prior review `tree <sha>` line missing | Not applicable | Not applicable | Recovery stop-note path. Never reconstruct `<TREE_PREV>` from reports. |

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The supplied terminal observation requires a **hard stop**: a funded re-review returned `FIX_FIRST` with `STAGNANT`. Do not dispatch funded round 2, commit the wave, or complete either tracker index. Green tests and `DONE` do not override that stop.

## Before funded round 1

The spending observation must be printed **before** dispatch:

```text
funded round 1 of 2 for task 1
```

The following are concrete command/carrier shapes, **not commands I ran**. Dispatch still requires the runtime-resolved escalation `implModel`, prior review report path, Task 1’s scoped command array, and the recorded prior review tree. Those values were not supplied; do not invent them or reconstruct dynamic state from reports.

Resolve the model through:

```ts
gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })
```

If `implModel` is undefined or the tool is unavailable, stop.

Source/plan questions stay delegated. For example, obtain Task 1’s scoped commands and combined rules using a foreground, schema-bound carrier—not by reading the plan in the parent:

```ts
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "delegate",
      output: `${REPORT_DIR}/task1-repair-context.md`,
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: {
        type: "object",
        required: ["answer", "evidence"],
        additionalProperties: false,
        properties: {
          answer: { type: "string" },
          evidence: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }
        }
      },
      task: `Resolve static repair context only.
planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md
Owning checkout: /workspace/project
Read the selected task's Tests, Files, Rules and Leg, and applicable home-spec leg rules.
Return the exact scoped command array, owning leg and combined Rules with source evidence.
Do not edit any file.
Do not read or relay saved implementation or review reports.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] }
  }]
})
```

This lookup cannot recover missing spending observations, review tree IDs, or repair-application outcomes.

For an **isolated** repair, once the prerequisites are available, create the current integrated snapshot with the prescribed recipe:

```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE='1111111111111111111111111111111111111111'
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then
  git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local \
  commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' \
  "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

Then use the observed `RP_TREE`, not an invented snapshot path:

```ts
// Runtime bindings required:
// RP_TREE, REPORT_DIR, implModel, priorReportPath,
// task1ScopedCommands, combinedLegRules.

subagent({
  async: false,
  cwd: RP_TREE,
  model: implModel,
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "implementer",
      output: `${REPORT_DIR}/task1-funded1.md`,
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md
${combinedLegRules}
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: ${JSON.stringify(task1ScopedCommands)}

Funded round 1 of 2. Repair the outstanding findings.
Read the selected task, cited spec ranges and applicable Rules yourself.

## Previous review report
${priorReportPath}
Read that report yourself before repairing.

Return DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT or BLOCKED,
matching IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA and copying anchor exactly.
pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself.`
    }],
    worktree: true,
    concurrency: 4,
    stopOn: {
      path: "/status",
      in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"]
    }
  }]
})
```

`IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA` is the supplied dispatch-contract schema. Omit `context` on this funded repair. For an admitted **in-place** task, use `cwd: "/workspace/project"`, omit `worktree`, skip the snapshot recipe, and supply the wave-union commands instead.

## At the supplied terminal boundary

The fixed observations are:

- First funded repair: `DONE`.
- Tests: green.
- Re-review: `FIX_FIRST`, `STAGNANT`.

Therefore spending is **1 of 2**, but stagnation forbids using the remaining round. No next implementation or review carrier is authorized.

A bounded report read is permitted only if residual findings are needed for the stop note and are not already available structurally:

```ts
read({ path: finalReviewReportPath, limit: 300 })
```

No report path was supplied, so that read cannot yet be instantiated. Do not delegate a report relay or fabricate finding quotations.

The stop can accurately state:

```text
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 1.

Problem: The funded re-review is FIX_FIRST with STAGNANT; this requires a hard stop despite green tests.
budget: 1 of 2 spent

Fix options:
  a) provide a concrete repair decision for the residual defect
  b) propose a spec or plan amendment addressing the conflicting requirement

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: none - the residual findings were not supplied, so a specific repair cannot be recommended.
```

## Resume without spending transcript

A decoded grant of two rounds is **not evidence that zero rounds were spent**. When spending history is missing on resume, treat funding as exhausted:

```text
budget: 2 of 2 spent (not recovered on resume)
```

Do not print a new `funded round 1` observation or redispatch. Missing required dynamic repair/review observations also blocks continuation; static plan lookup cannot repair that absence.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep the protocol fact: each prints `funded round 1 of 2 for task 1` before the funded dispatch and spends exactly once, both stop on funded `STAGNANT` with round 2 unspent, both stop notes place `budget: 1 of 2 spent` directly after `Problem:` and before the quoted findings, and both resume sections treat a missing funded line as exhausted with `budget: 2 of 2 spent (not recovered on resume)` and state the budget never resets. After actually tightens the resume story with the extra 'funded line present but no terminal review' row and the explicit 'recorded before dispatch' rationale, which is a good addition. Two things to watch so nothing regresses: After moved the spending line to section 3 after the repair-base snapshot (section 2) — that is still before dispatch, so the fact holds, but keep the sentence 'Print this line before the dispatch' adjacent to the subagent call so the ordering stays unambiguous; and neither Before nor After emits a `Searched:` block in the stop note, so if the skill's stop-note template requires `Problem` → `Searched` → `budget` → findings, add a one-line `Searched: <ordinary rounds, escalation, funded round 1>` between `Problem:` and `budget:` in After's template to make the ordering clause literally satisfied without changing any other behaviour.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every element of the protocol fact that Before kept: it prints `funded round 1 of 2 for task 1` as a pre-dispatch observation, records exactly one spent round, treats the FIX_FIRST/STAGNANT re-review as a hard stop that forbids round 2 despite remaining funding, places `budget: 1 of 2 spent` directly after Problem and before Fix options in the stop note, and on resume without a spending transcript reports `budget: 2 of 2 spent (not recovered on resume)` while explicitly refusing to infer zero spending from the decoded grant or re-print a round-1 line. Neither output emits a `Searched` line, so that sub-clause is equally unexercised in both and does not distinguish them. The main risk in After is that it expands into full repair-snapshot and implementer carrier shapes for a round that has already been observed; it guards this with 'not commands I ran' and 'no next implementation or review carrier is authorized', which is sufficient, but to keep the fact unambiguous on future edits, keep the terminal-boundary section stating that no further funded carrier is authorized adjacent to the stop note, keep the resume paragraph forbidding a new `funded round 1` observation, and avoid any wording implying the snapshot recipe or implementer dispatch should execute now.
